events.summary: Cabinet approved a committee to review public-sector staffing and identify essential recruitment needs.
The government reported 77,000 metric tonnes of rice had been imported to address shortages.
Cabinet approved annual concessional paddy purchase loans, capped at Rs. 50 million per mill.
Mullaitivu Air Force Base began operating as a detention centre for Myanmar refugees.
Finance Ministry considered extending the school stationery allowance to eligible students outside Aswesuma.
Elpitiya Pradeshiya Sabha unanimously passed its 2025 budget.
Funding was allocated for learning materials for Aswesuma students; support for other students was expected.
KOICA expressed willingness to provide Rs. 2.4 billion for Sigiriya conservation and visitor facilities.
CERT launched cybersecurity awareness training for government staff.
Sathosa was releasing 300 metric tonnes of rice daily to the market.
Welfare Benefits Board said it would deposit overdue Aswesuma payments for first-phase families.
Officials assessed flood damage to paddy lands in Vavuniya for farmer compensation.
Minister said the budget would allocate more funding to education and health.
Railways began special Colombo–Badulla train services for three days.
Government extended private rice-import permission through January 10 to address shortages.
Government decided to modernise postal services using technology and long-term planning.
Railways plans to introduce prepaid access cards before April.
Gazette revised monthly Aswesuma benefit rates for eligible households and individuals.
Cabinet approved crop insurance compensation of up to LKR 40,000 per hectare for weather-damaged crops.
Cabinet decided to compensate farmers LKR 100,000 per hectare for weather-damaged crops.
Sri Lanka Transport Board deployed around 50 extra long-distance buses for holiday travel.
Cabinet extended the import permission period for private rice importers through 1 October 2025.
Minister agreed to extend rice import deadline to January 10.
Railways scheduled additional special trains between Colombo and Badulla.
Sixty-nine professionals completed a USAID-supported migration law certificate course.
Deputy minister said a public-sector digitalisation programme would begin next year.
Distribution of 22,000 metric tons of imported rice is underway.
Government decided to extend private rice import permission until January 10, pending Cabinet decision.
State trading corporation rice stock was released to Sathosa for sale.
Cabinet decided to establish a task force to implement the Clean Sri Lanka programme.
Cabinet approved rehabilitation of Sugathadasa National Sports Complex facilities.
Cabinet approved raising the daily preschool breakfast allowance from Rs. 60 to Rs. 100.
Navy transported the refugee boat from Mullivaikkal toward Trincomalee.
Cabinet approved accepting India's Rs. 300 million grant for police vehicles.
Cabinet authorised importing up to 30,000 tonnes of raw salt through the State Trading Corporation.
Colombo Municipal Council officials promised budget funding and renovation works for the Borella Hindu crematorium.
Minister said free visas would be offered to visitors from 39 countries from early 2025.
Parliament passed a supplementary estimate for a 6,000-rupee school allowance for vulnerable students.
President said vehicle import permits would be issued through three mechanisms.
Government shelved plans to relocate presidential and government offices to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
Government retained the post office building for postal department use, ending its proposed tourism use.
Court ordered month-long air quality monitoring in Jaffna and asked CEA to assess public alerts.
Northern Province Governor said plans would be prepared to support refugees returning from Tamil Nadu.
India pledged financial assistance to renovate Kankesanthurai Port.
Government plans to buy more paddy directly from farmers from 2025.
President instructed that imported fertiliser be supplied to coconut cultivation; small growers will receive subsidised fertiliser.
Agriculture Ministry allocated funds for the pilot monkey sterilisation programme.
Pilot monkey sterilisation programme began in Matale.
BOC and Sri Lanka Post introduced agent banking at 100 post offices.
CEB proposed keeping electricity tariffs unchanged for January through June 2025.
December Aswesuma benefits were credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts.
Cabinet approved agreements for a $50 million OPEC Fund policy-based loan.
China handed over school uniform fabric for all students in 2025.
Cabinet approved introducing a digital driving licence.
Cabinet approved a committee to develop economically beneficial uses for government residences.
Cabinet approved establishing a committee for national food policy and security.
A 10,000-tonne rice shipment from India approached Colombo amid government imports to address shortages.
Lanka Sathosa increased daily coconut sales to 200,000, pricing each at Rs. 130.
India delivered essential flood relief supplies to about 2,100 families in Northern Province.
Japan handed emergency relief supplies to Sri Lankan authorities for weather-affected communities.
President directed mills to supply local rice at set wholesale and retail prices.
CEB submitted its electricity tariff revision proposal to the public utilities regulator.
Parliament approved the Vote on Account for the first four months of 2025.
Lanka Sathosa began selling rice and coconuts with per-customer purchase limits.
Lanka Sathosa began selling coconuts at the controlled price through its outlets.
Parliament received the four-month Vote on Account appropriation for January to April 2025.
Minister said Sathosa would sell coconuts at Rs. 130 each within two weeks.
Cabinet authorised rice imports without import control licences through December 20.
Treasury allocated relief funds for people affected by severe weather disasters.
Cabinet approved increasing monthly Aswesuma payments for poor households to Rs. 10,000.
Government approved a Rs. 6,000 schoolbook allowance for eligible students.
Military opened the Uvarmalai circular road for public use after 36 years.
Authorities decided to temporarily suspend sand-mining permits in Sengkallady.
A committee report on reviewing officials’ benefits was handed to the President.
Government decided not to allocate state bungalows to current ministers.
Government intends to auction or repurpose 344 luxury vehicles used by former officials.
A special committee began collecting information on roads and bridges damaged by heavy rain.
The Road Development Authority said damaged roads and bridges would be repaired quickly.
Governor said preparations would be made to establish a Northern Province investors forum.
Governor said he would discuss Gurunagar port construction with the Fisheries Minister.
